title: Market Pulse: Treasury Pressure Outlasts the AI Selloff
summary: Pre-open equities are mixed as Treasury yields and the dollar remain elevated; AI leadership uncertainty persists while producer-price inflation is the next test. Verification pending: source-based automated review, not human claim-by-claim sign-off.
reviewed_by: BLAQUE BAUX automated research; human verification pending

sections.heading: What Happened: Observed Facts
paragraphs: At 5:42 a.m. EST, S&P 500 futures were up 0.12%, Dow futures up 0.21% and Nasdaq 100 futures down 0.13%, according to TipRanks. These are premarket observations, not cash-session returns.

Reuters reported European equities near recent records and the dollar close to a 19-month high as investors assessed the possibility of a larger December Federal Reserve rate increase. U.S. yields remained under upward pressure.

Thursday's AI selloff followed Nvidia's CEO transition, with Colette Kress serving as interim chief executive. The company-specific shock has not established a comparable deterioration in all AI end-market demand.

October producer-price inflation is due at 8:30 a.m. EST; the reported consensus is a 0.4% monthly headline increase. This edition precedes the release. Current synchronized issuer CDS, broad credit spreads and cash VIX readings were not independently established.

sections.heading: What Mattered: Interpretation
paragraphs: Since Thursday afternoon, the most important shift is not a new AI demand datapoint but the continued pressure from yields and monetary-policy expectations while equity futures show only modest stabilization.

Higher benchmark yields can increase refinancing and project hurdle rates even when chip orders remain strong. Suppliers, data-center borrowers, utilities and customers may experience different cash-flow consequences.

sections.heading: What We're Watching
list: 8:30 a.m. EST producer-price release; compare actual headline and core figures with consensus before drawing conclusions.
Two-year and 10-year Treasury yields, dollar reaction and December Fed pricing after PPI.
Nvidia succession disclosures and customer commitments; distinguish governance concerns from operational disruption.
Corporate credit spreads, AI-linked issuer refinancing costs and actual cash conversion.
Crude and Gulf shipping conditions; separate physical supply disruption from geopolitical risk premium.

sections.heading: Where We See Things Going
paragraphs: If producer-price inflation undershoots expectations and credit spreads remain contained, selective stabilization becomes more plausible. If inflation surprises upward and long yields climb further, financing-sensitive AI infrastructure operators could remain vulnerable. Neither path warrants a precise probability or index target from the evidence available.

signal: BLAQUE BAUX Signal: Equity stabilization is not equivalent to cheaper capital. The next test is whether inflation and credit pricing permit AI infrastructure cash flows to support the financing behind expansion.
